finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST 'feed' parameter is passed to file_get_contents, allowing attacker-chosen URLs to be fetched server-side. No scheme, host, or auth validation. HTTP redirects are followed by default. Only the response length is returned, so this is blind-style SSRF rated MEDIUM.

trace.note: isset($_POST['feed']) gates on POST and key presence only
file_get_contents($_POST['feed']) dispatches the outbound fetch with the raw user value
echo strlen($xml) returns response length to the caller (side-channel oracle)

finding.guards_checked: No session or admin check on this path. No scheme restriction. No host allowlist or filter_var/URL parsing. Redirects followed by PHP http wrapper with no re-validation. Not closed by any guard.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only checks on this path are the REQUEST_METHOD === 'POST' and isset($_POST['feed']) gate at import.php:11. The require_admin() check at import.php:4-9 is only called from the set_webhook branch at import.php:18, not the feed branch. No scheme, host, or URL validation exists before file_get_contents at import.php:12.
verdict.reason: The raw $_POST['feed'] value at import.php:11 is passed straight to file_get_contents at import.php:12 with no authentication or URL validation, and the response length is echoed back at import.php:13, so an unauthenticated attacker can make the server fetch arbitrary URLs and observe the response size.

finding.claim: Admin-only set_webhook parameter is passed to curl_init and curl_exec with no URL validation. Response body is discarded (blind SSRF). Redirects are not followed (CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION unset). Rated MEDIUM because the only gate is admin auth, which does not close SSRF to internal targets. Exposure is higher if is_admin can be set from user input, which could not be verified from this codebase.
finding.sink: curl_init($hook) at import.php:20 with curl_exec($ch) at import.php:22

trace.note: curl_init($hook) sets the target URL with no scheme or host check
curl_exec($ch) performs the outbound request; response discarded, 'ok' echoed

finding.guards_checked: require_admin() session check (authorization, not a URL allowlist; does not close SSRF per skill rules). No scheme validation. No host allowlist. No IP/CIDR blocking. Redirects not followed by default. Setter of $_SESSION['is_admin'] not present in this codebase, so it could not be verified.

verdict.guard_found: none closing. require_admin() at import.php:4-9 gates the path (called at line 18), but it is an authorization check, not a URL validation guard. There is no scheme or host check on $hook before curl_init at line 20.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code (import.php:18-22), but the source fails the attacker-controlled test: $_POST['set_webhook'] is only reachable after require_admin() at import.php:18 passes, so only an admin can supply the URL, which is not an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker. The candidate itself says the is_admin setter could not be checked, so whether a low-privilege user can reach this path is unverified, and that is the only route to a finding. Separately, import.php:11-12 passes an unauthenticated $_POST['feed'] straight to file_get_contents with no validation, which is a more serious SSRF-style sink that the candidate did not report.
